title: Delinquency, Treasury Cross-Servicing Referral and Credit Reporting — Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery Standard
content:
## Referral

A debt in **Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery** is referred to Treasury cross-servicing when all three of these hold:

- it has been delinquent for more than the debt type's referral delinquency period;
- it is not on hold or in a repayment plan;
- its balance is at least the debt type's smallest referred balance.

Treasury then adds its cross-servicing fee: the debt type's fee percentage of the referred balance, rounded to the cent.

**Days delinquent** are counted from the initial notice date, or from the date the last plan installment or hold ended if that is later, to the current date; they are the calendar days on which the debt was active and no direct payment or benefit offset was posted on it.

## After referral

A referred debt can be collected from federal tax refunds; from Social Security benefits, no more than the debt type's Social Security percentage and never from the protected first amount of a monthly benefit; from federal salary, no more than the federal salary percentage of disposable pay; and by administrative wage garnishment, no more than the garnishment percentage of disposable pay. Once referred, VA no longer sets up plans or takes compromise offers on the debt; the debtor deals with Treasury.

## Credit bureaus and demand letters

A delinquent debt of a type that is reported to the consumer credit bureaus is reported once the type's reporting period has passed since the notice; other debt types are never reported. The second demand letter goes out the debt type's follow-up period after the notice when there is no response.

## Referral test (truth table)

| Delinquent beyond the period | On hold or in a plan | Balance at least the smallest referred balance | Referred |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | No | Yes | Yes |
| Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| Yes | No | No | No |
| No | No | Yes | No |

**Hypothetical fee.** A referred balance of 2,345.67 USD at a fee of 32.0 percent gives 750.6144 USD, rounded to the cent: 750.61 USD added to the balance.
